layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: The entire area of Sikkim is a Protected Area (Third Schedule, Immigration and Foreigners Order 2025). Every foreigner needs a permit to enter or stay; Sikkim Tourism still calls the basic entry permit a Restricted Area Permit (RAP). Since the MHA letter of 17 December 2024, all PAP/RAP applications go through e-FRRO (indianfrro.gov.in) only, with no physical permits. Indian missions advise approval 30 days ahead with the visa, or 15 days ahead via the FRRO if already in India.

layers.authority: Ministry of Home Affairs, Government of India (e-FRRO portal)
layers.process: Khunphenling Tibetan settlement at Rabangla (South Sikkim) is a Restricted Area under the Fourth Schedule. Daytime visits are allowed without a permit if the settlement, monastery or institute gives the visitor's name, parentage, date of birth, nationality, passport and visa numbers to the Foreigners Registration Officer. Staying needs a Restricted Area Permit; foreign students can get one valid for 3 years if the institute vouches for them. Where a whole state is covered, as in Sikkim, a permit for a Tibetan settlement or monastery doesn't replace the Protected Area Permit for the state.

layers.authority: Department of Tourism and Civil Aviation, Government of Sikkim
layers.process: Sikkim Tourism's RAP page says the basic permit is free and lists permit offices (Tourism Information Centres at Reshi, Rambam and Pakyong as named on the page, and the Tourist Information Centre at Bagdogra). With it, foreigners may visit for tourism: North (Phodong, Mangan, Singhik up to Toong), South (Namchi, Ravangla), West (Gyalshing, Soreng, Pemayangtse, Khecheopalri, Tashiding, Yuksom) and East (Gangtok, Rumtek, Pakyong, Rongli, Rhenock, Aritar, Rorathang). Stay up to 30 days, extendable to 60 in total. Register within 24 hours of arrival. People born in, or nationals of, Myanmar or Nigeria need prior clearance; Pakistan, Afghanistan, China (including Hong Kong and Macau) need MHA approval first.

layers.authority: Department of Tourism and Civil Aviation, Government of Sikkim
layers.process: Tsomgo Lake (East Sikkim) needs a Protected Area Permit for a day trip. Lachen, Lachung, Yumthang and Thangu (North Sikkim) need a PAP for a minimum of 3 days and 2 nights and a maximum of 5 days and 4 nights, supervised by a registered guide. Foreigners must apply through a Sikkim Tourism registered travel agent in groups of two or more. Nathula Pass and Gurudongmar Lake are not open to foreigners. Motorbikes must be 150 cc or more to enter PAP areas.

zone-requirements.note: Sikkim Tourism's RAP page still describes paper forms at permit offices, but the MHA letter of 17 December 2024 and a January 2026 state notice (reported) moved all foreigner permits to e-FRRO only. Treat the office list as places to ask, and apply on e-FRRO. Sikkim's tourism pages read only via search snapshots (the site loads its text by script). Khunphenling Tibetan settlement at Rabangla is also a Restricted Area under the Fourth Schedule.

laws.rule: The whole of Sikkim is a Protected Area: a foreigner must hold a permit to enter or stay. The civil authority can attach conditions, including reporting to police and limits on surveying, sketching or photography.

Foreigners (except people of Bhutanese origin) need a RAP/PAP, from Indian missions with the visa, online via e-FRRO (about ₹2,880 (about A$42.95 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026) per head, 3 to 15 working days) or free at border counters in emergencies only. Register with the Foreigners Registration Office within 24 hours of arrival. Initial validity up to 30 days, extendable by 30. Tsomgo Lake (day trip) and Lachen, Lachung, Yumthang and Thangu need a PAP; North Sikkim permits run 3 days/2 nights to 5 days/4 nights, via a registered agent, groups of 2 or more.

laws.rule: Sikkim’s pollution control board says PET bottles of packaged drinking water of two litres or less are prohibited; a May 2026 enforcement notice reports inspections in Gangtok, Mangan, Nayabazar-Jorethang, Rangpo, Singtam and Gyalshing. Check current local rules before carrying packaged water.

laws.rule: Sikkim’s May 2026 plastic-enforcement notice lists prohibited single-use items including plastic plates, cups, glasses, cutlery, straws and stirrers. The notice reports enforcement in named municipalities; check the current rules for the place visited.
